The (r,Q) continuous-review policy with reorder point 902 and order quantity 4,698 is capacity-constrained (max storage 5,127.8 units), reducing the unconstrained EOQ of 6,469 by 27%. research_insights.selection_rationale: With near-continuous daily demand (95.2% non-zero days) and volatile lead times, a continuous-review reorder-point / fixed-order-quantity model is the most appropriate. It triggers replenishment immediately when stock hits the reorder point, minimising exposure to lead time uncertainty without requiring periodic review overhead.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity binds at 5,127.8 units, capping the order quantity 27% below the economic optimum. This raises order frequency and ordering cost marginally, and leaves only 0.8 units of slack in the storage constraint. Any safety stock increase would require a corresponding OQ reduction, further degrading cost efficiency. Physical capacity expansion is recommended.
